A.explanation: The island is a territory under the parent's enforced national regime: the binary passport rule, entry-discrepancy cable, fraud-ineligibility lever, airport screening and federal facilities/custody policy all apply at the border and in federal settings, and the island hosts a large federal military presence subject to the service-member ban. Local law is more protective than the parent: unanimous employment protection covering gender identity (2015), same-sex marriage recognition, no local sodomy statute since 1978, and documented island-wide LGBTQ tolerance with a visible scene and Pride — though the attitudinal record is general-LGBTQ, not trans-specific, and gender recognition requires surgery. No local trans-specific violence or police targeting is documented, but the dossier is thin there. Compared with the hostile parent average, the island's documented local acceptance and protective employment law lift it above the parent; the universal federal border/document exposures and federal custody regime cap it well below the Reduced band's top.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal passport rules apply: binary sex markers per assigned birth sex, X markers discontinued, entry cable flags document discrepancies and contemplates lifetime fraud findings; documented confiscations and strandings of trans travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; passport policy is under active court challenge.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal screening and entry govern arrival regardless of island's local tolerance.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau 2026 policies (hair cutting, hormone removal, described conversion therapy) and documented immigration-custody abuse of trans men apply to federal custody on the island.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Federal detention regime reaches any arrest handed to federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Parent order bars trans access to federally funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; military presence subjects federal personnel on-island to the service ban.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No island-level facility ban documented; local culture tolerant.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities operate under parent rules inside a tolerant territory.

care_services.exposure: No island care restriction documented; parent measures on minors' care are contested or enjoined.
care_services.protection: Tolerant local health environment implied but not trans-specifically documented.
care_services.interaction: Parent health rules could reach federally funded settings.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Parent counterterrorism framing of 'radical gender ideology' applies nationally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No island police targeting of trans people documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal speech/enforcement posture overlays a locally tolerant police environment.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parent minors' care restrictions and school-prosecution order remain in force or contested; island gender recognition requires surgery.
minors_guardians.protection: Local acceptance culture; local employment protections extend to trans people.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor meets federal document and care layers plus the island's tolerant social layer.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence data identified for the island — absence of evidence, not evidence of safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Documented island-wide LGBTQ acceptance, visible scene since the 1990s, annual Pride; federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Societal tolerance documented only as general-LGBTQ, not trans-specific.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Thin trans-specific record on policing, violence and healthcare on-island.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Unanimous local employment anti-discrimination statute (2015); marriage recognition; contested federal litigation may soften parent rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse for border/federal matters runs through the parent's contested courts.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A's register bars trans visitors at the border with no remedy. The island shares the parent's border/document exposure but adds no local bar, plus documented local acceptance and a protective employment statute — above 0.35-A.

0.55-B's secondary screening is administrative delay with functioning appeal desks. The island's federal border layer is harsher than that, but its documented local tolerance is stronger than 0.55-B's; net comparable, slightly above.

0.75-C has trained border officers, appeal tribunal, release and compensation. The island's federal layer is materially worse (binary markers, fraud lever, custody harms); it cannot reach 0.75-C despite local tolerance.

A.synthesis: The operative regime is two-layered. The federal layer imposes universal-exposure exposures — binary passports, discrepancy-driven refusals, potential fraud ineligibility, federal facility and custody harms, military ban applying on-island — which no visitor avoids. The island layer is genuinely protective for local life: unanimous gender-identity employment protection, marriage recognition, decriminalised sodomy since 1978, and documented island-wide LGBTQ acceptance with a visible scene and Pride. The island's tolerance raises it above the parent's hostile national average, but the attitudinal record is general-LGBTQ rather than trans-specific, trans-specific violence data is absent, and the border remains the parent's regime — so the score sits mid-scale, around 0.52, not in the Reduced band's upper range.

B.explanation: The state layers its own hostile regime on the parent's. The 2023 gubernatorial order fixes sex at birth for all state agencies, ends state recognition of trans identity, and backs single-sex spaces; locally issued documents require surgery; care for anyone under 19 is banned and upheld by the state supreme court, so a visitor travelling with a trans minor cannot obtain care and the school-prosecution order targets facilitation of a minor's transition. Custody is a documented harm: a trans woman was celled with a male sex offender who assaulted her and the court dismissed her claims, dismissing the assault as de minimis — institutions themselves enforcing birth-sex placement without remedy. No state gender-identity hate-crime or anti-discrimination statute exists; recourse is federal only. Combined with the parent's binary-passport and fraud-lever exposures, this sits at the High-Risk band's floor: state-imposed universal exposure with thin working remedy, softened only by marriage/adoption recognition, national hate-crime coverage and litigation.

entry_documents.exposure: Parent binary passport rules, X-marker elimination, discrepancy cable with lifetime fraud-ineligibility lever, and documented confiscations/strandings apply to every arrival.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; passport policy under court challenge.
entry_documents.interaction: State surgical-marker requirements for local documents compound the parent regime for anyone needing state ID.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: trans woman housed in men's prison, celled with a male sex offender who sexually assaulted her; district judge dismissed failure-to-treat, surgery-denial and failure-to-protect claims as de minimis. Federal corrections/ICE custody harms also documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None working; the court endorsed the placement.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Local arrest routes into birth-sex custody; federal custody adds its own documented abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Governor's 2023 order fixes sex at birth and backs single-sex bathrooms/changing rooms for state agencies; parent order bars congruent access in federally funded facilities; no facility-use enforcement provision recorded for the state.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State and federal facility definitions align against congruent access.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care banned for anyone under 19 (2023, upheld 6-1 in 2024); a visitor of any age cannot obtain it for a minor in their care.
care_services.protection: National fair-housing/employment coverage; one city's public-accommodation ordinance.
care_services.interaction: Travelling families face care denial with state inquiry risk for facilitation.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State executive order ends recognition of trans identity; parent counterterrorism framing of 'radical gender ideology'; first-known bathroom-trespass arrest occurred in a peer state with handcuffing and 24h men's-ward holding.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 1997 state hate-crime law operates (2016 precedent) but excludes gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing aligned with parent hostility; no state-level trans protection.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-19 care ban; parent school order directs criminal prosecution of those facilitating a minor's social transition; athletics banned for trans students; sports/athletics identity policing.
minors_guardians.protection: Name-change publication shortened for minors; marriage/adoption recognition; national hate-crime statute covers GI.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian exposure: the penalised facilitation act attaches to the adult, not only the minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state trans-victimisation statistics recorded — absence of evidence; local discrimination protection absent, so remedy for harassment rests on federal law.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime law exists but omits gender identity; federal statute covers GI.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims must rely on national charging where state law is silent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Court dismissed the documented custody case without remedy; state anti-discrimination ordinance in one city was repealed by petition; several parent measures enjoined — operative position unstable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation against passport policy ongoing; federal fair-housing enforcement accepting trans complaints.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Oversight exists but the record shows enforcement not changing outcomes for trans people.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-B's police stop-and-question with fines and no credible imprisonment resembles this state's friction, but here custody harm is documented with judicial endorsement and the care ban reaches families — comparable, slightly worse.

0.25-C is birth-sex prison placement with assaults and dismissals — the state's documented custody case matches that tier exactly; the state adds the minors' care ban but retains federal protections, so slightly above 0.25-C.

0.75-C has functioning border remedies, counsel and compensation. Here remedies were dismissed, state law strips recognition and no working state recourse exists — the state is materially below 0.75-C.

B.synthesis: The combined regime is the parent's hostile national layer plus an actively hostile state layer. Universal exposures reach every traveller: binary documents, discrepancy-driven refusal and fraud leverage at entry, facility definitions fixing sex at birth at both state and federal levels. The documented custody case — assault in a men's facility followed by judicial dismissal as de minimis — shows the institutions enforcing hostile placement without remedy, a tier-1 exposure under the rubric. For travelling families the under-19 care ban and the school-facilitation prosecution order create guardian-facing legal exposure. Mitigations — marriage and adoption recognition, federal hate-crime coverage, one city ordinance, ongoing litigation — are real but thin and largely non-state-operating. The state sits at the floor of the High-Risk band, around 0.30.
